Village feels smaller today. Not bad small.
That dog by the mill ignored me. Twice.
Clouds are stuck. No wind. Unusual.
I fixed the lantern on our gate. It was loose.
Errands are done. All of them. Suspicious.
Grass in the square is overgrown. Should report it.
Report it to who? Nobody. Forget I said it.
A kid waved at me. I waved back correctly this time.
Progress. Slow progress. Still progress.
I stood by the pond for eleven minutes. Did nothing.
It was fine. Doing nothing is fine. Sometimes.
The ducks have a leader. I respect that.
Someone's laundry is out. Blue bedsheets.
I know too much about this village. Can't leave now.
The inn changed its sign. New font. Worse font.
I have opinions about fonts. You know this.
There's a bench by the orchard with my name on it?
Not literally. Someone carved initials. N.T.
Could be another N.T. Statistically possible.
I sat there anyway. Good bench.
The cheese stall is closed Fridays. Noted.
Noted for no reason. I don't buy cheese.
I might buy cheese. That's a decision later.
Saw a cat with three legs. It outran me.
I wasn't chasing. It was just faster. Somehow.
Kids are playing tag near the well. Loud.
I watched for a minute. Reminded me of my build test.
Both involve a lot of falling down and trying again.
That's a metaphor. Don't write it down.
The blacksmith's hammer is off rhythm today.
I noticed because I'm always listening. Occupational thing.
Occupational? No. Just habit. Nothing deeper.
Flowers on the south path are new. Purple ones.
I didn't pick any. I thought about it.
Thought about it and left them. That's all.
Your chair on the porch has a wobble.
I fixed the wobble. It took one nail.
No big deal. The nail was right there.
The well water tastes like pennies today.
Copper. It's fine. Probably fine.
I drank some anyway. Still standing.
Saw a fox near the chicken coop. No casualties.
The fox looked embarrassed. I respect that.
It ran off before I could judge it properly.
The town crier has a cold. He whispered the news.
It was quieter. I preferred it. Don't tell him.
Tomorrow's market moved to the east field. Heard it.
Heard it from the baker. The baker hears everything.
Bakers are the real informants of this village.
I should be one. My code goes stale overnight.
That's a joke. Half of one. You decide which half.
The clock tower ran three minutes fast. I fixed it.
You didn't ask. I know. I'm telling you anyway.
Fixed it meant I tapped the glass. It worked.
Don't look at me like that. It worked.
A pigeon followed me to the square.
It stopped when I stopped. That's a glitch.
I checked. Real pigeons do that. Still weird.
There's a puddle shaped like a crescent moon.
I almost took a picture. Then remembered I have no camera.
